title: Phase-Uniform Studentized Inference for Joint-Cap Estimators across Face and Corner Regimes
banked_reason: D0.5 rejected the substituted kernel; the original positive honest-length lower bound is false at the allowed sigma_min=1/2 endpoint.
gap_reasons: The core delivers asymptotic studentized coverage and an O_P length bound only, while the proposal promised a finite-sample honest interval and matched minimax risk/length; restore that promised object or explicitly reframe the contribution as the narrower covariance-law result.

The negative theorem refutes a newly defined projection-variance oracle, but does not name a specific published estimator or workflow (bibkey plus its claimed guarantee) that uses this calibration; its comparison to Abadie--Imbens fixed-geometry matching is not a targetable refutation.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a phase-uniform covariance and studentization argument for a shared-donor joint-cap estimator, then strengthened it with a projection-oracle undercoverage claim. D0.5 found that this replaced the promised finite-sample matched minimax risk and honest expected-length kernel; independent review also found two unresolved proof gaps in the narrower result. At the allowed sigma_min=1/2 endpoint, the class has a known constant target and admits a zero-length honest interval, so the proposed positive honest-length lower bound is false without changing the parameter restriction.
tldr: A single observable exact-covariance studentizer remains valid as uncertainty moves among the regular, two face, and corner components of the causal joint-cap estimator. The proof covers random donor counts, empty cells, every shared face-corner coefficient, polynomial inverse-CDF geometry, and pilot residual replacement without density smoothness or a logarithmic loss. A legal Bernoulli product-density face witness additionally proves an inferential failure: the one-observation Hájek projection omits a public positive fraction of the exact variance, so even its oracle nominal interval has limiting coverage strictly below \(1-\alpha\).
gap: The established joint-cap package determines the four component orders but gives only conservative Markov calibration. Published matching limit theory fixes the matching geometry, scalar bias-aware inference has no shared face--corner covariance, and Chen and Gao's version 3 already permits known or unknown submanifold mappings and nonlinear or moving upper-contour functionals. None addresses cap-generated weights under polynomial boundary thinning with shared-donor covariance that survives phase ties.
fill: Under the paper-specific full-domain coordinate Hölder restriction, the project derives a uniform Hájek expansion, identifies the full varying covariance target, supplies a total residual-based shared-donor studentizer, and proves pointwise-in-cap coverage uniformly over the complete polynomial tail-speed field and its transition neighborhoods.
